title: Invisible in plain sight.
excerpt: Three days at NCAEC, more than 40 exhibitors, and a new view of the connections happening on the show floor.
image_alt: Attendees and exhibitors on the NCAEC show floor
source_note: Adapted from our September 2026 newsletter. Added to the archive October 1, 2026.
body_html:
In late July, Evential completed its first full deployment at NCAEC. Across three days and more than 40 exhibitors, we helped an event that had been running for eight years see a part of its story it had not previously been able to measure: what happened on the floor.

Built to fit the event

Attendees scanned once and wore a lanyard. There was no app to download, and the measurement did not require them to interrupt their conversations with exhibitors.

You were invisible in plain sight.

Richard, NCAEC Executive Director

What the numbers revealed

As reported in our September newsletter, 88% of attendees visited a sponsor booth, 68% were qualified leads, and 72% returned to the same booth at least twice. These results gave the organizers a more detailed picture than attendance alone.

Location and behavior told another story. Corner booths saw more flow than edge booths, and one exhibitor recorded more than twice the median engagement despite paying the same price. Measurement made those differences visible.

Evidence sponsors could take home

Within days of the show, each monitored exhibitor received a report covering traffic and leads. The event included companies such as Milwaukee Tool, Brady, Emerson, Capital Electric, Current Tools, and nVent CADDY.

For the organizing team, the ambition was to make the event the place to be in July. The deployment offered a way to connect that ambition with evidence of the interactions the show created.

What came next

The September update also pointed to the expansion of Evential’s sponsor discovery experience, with free browsing and more updates ahead. The central lesson stayed the same: the strongest event stories are easier to tell when the floor itself can supply the evidence.

title: The first Evential dashboard is live.
excerpt: From manually exported prototype data to a platform for organizers and sponsors: a look back at the April 5 release.
source_note: Adapted from our April 2026 newsletter. Added to the archive October 1, 2026.
body_html:
On April 5, we shipped the first iteration of the Evential dashboard. It marked a shift from manually exporting prototype data to giving organizers and sponsors a platform where they could explore their event.

An overview of the event floor

The release brought check-ins, foot traffic, dwell time, and booth visits into a live overview, with support for multiple events. The goal was to make activity on the floor easier to understand while the event was still unfolding.

A clearer view for sponsors

The April update introduced a sponsor report marketplace and a report experience covering leads, engagement scores, dwell time, and repeat visits, with CSV and PDF exports. Organizers could offer qualified reports, with notifications supporting the process.

Next on the roadmap: automations

Automations were still coming soon in this update. The planned workflows would connect live event triggers to actions, including webhooks and tools such as Zapier and Make.

This milestone — deploying and publishing our first iteration — is one of many to come. I look forward to many more late nights with messy desks.

Rohan Tyagi

Still a lot to build and improve going forward, but this is a big milestone for Evential.

Rithul Saravanakumar

At the time, we were preparing for the next pilot and opening conversations about our pre-seed round. The dashboard gave those conversations something tangible: a first product built around what we had learned on the floor.

title: From prototype to proof.
excerpt: Twenty days, one live deployment, and the first evidence of what event organizers could learn from the floor.
image_alt: Evential’s first deployment at the INtercollegiate Entrepreneurship Summit
source_note: Adapted from our February 2026 newsletter. Added to the archive October 1, 2026.
body_html:
On Super Bowl night, an opportunity arrived: could Evential deploy at the INtercollegiate Entrepreneurship Summit on February 27? The event was 19 days away. The team took the prototype to 16 Tech in Indianapolis and put it to work at a real event.

What the first deployment showed

The gap between registration and attendance was 39%. Attendees traveled an average of 50.4 miles, compared with 61.8 miles for people who did not attend. That was an early observation worth exploring, rather than a forecast of who would show up next time.

At the end of the event, 59 meals remained untouched: $507 in catering spend. These were concrete examples of the uncertainty organizers face when planning against registration counts alone.

A small badge, a bigger ambition

The deployment used discreet smart badges without asking attendees to download an app. It gave the team a first view of how measurement could fit into an event’s existing flow.

We don’t want to be known as the guys who make smart badges. We want to be the world’s first real-time Event Intelligence platform — the all-in-one assistant to event organizers, eliminating uncertainty as events evolve.

The Evential team, February 2026

Building the next version

Rohan Tyagi, Rithul Saravanakumar, and Samarth Das helped make this first deployment possible. The February update also outlined plans for private connectivity, tamper-resistant hardware, and a live dashboard, alongside the search for founding engineers and pilot partners.

The first deployment was a starting point: move from a working prototype to evidence an organizer could actually use.
